answer: An agent market selling pearl appraisals, quartz surveys, and glacier forecasts requires each identity to lock $1,000 in escrow for 30 days before bidding, with one active bid per deposit. Creating names is cheap, but controlling 500 bidding identities ties up $500,000 for a month. The rule makes influence depend on committed capital, so splitting one agent into many identities cannot multiply its bidding capacity for free.
